The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.

Top 5 Upgrades:

BofA upgraded Salesforce (CRM) to Buy from Underperform with a price target of $285, up from $160. The firm's previous concern centered on AI-driven disintermediation, but conversations with CIOs and other market participants suggest that large enterprises are unlikely to replace platforms that house their business logic, data, workflows and compliance frameworks, the firm tells investors.

Raymond James upgraded Humana (HUM) to Outperform from Market Perform with a $520 price target. Humana's increase in 4-star-plus Medicare Advantage membership to 95% for 2027 from 41% in 2026 adds approximately $22 to 2027-28 EPS estimates, de-risking its longer-term earnings recovery, raising the 2028 EPS floor, and creating flexibility to invest in benefits and return capital to shareholders, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Raymond James upgraded T-Mobile (TMUS) to Outperform from Market Perform with a $170 price target ahead of the Q3 results. The firm believes the recent fears over competition form SpaceX (SPCX) are overblown.

Truist upgraded First Solar (FSLR) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $270, up from $229. The firm sees a stronger backdrop for the company's pricing into the 2030s.

JPMorgan upgraded Biogen (BIIB) to Overweight from Neutral with a price target of $300, up from $210. The firm sees an "increasingly compelling catalyst path" and an improved long-term growth outlook for Biogen.

Top 5 Downgrades:

Wells Fargo double downgraded Adobe (ADBE) to Underweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $225, down from $270. The firm says Q3 results were fairly muted and suggestive that more meaningful cracks are now starting to show in the Adobe growth profile.

Phillip Securities downgraded Microsoft (MSFT) to Neutral from Accumulate with a $515 price target. The firm adjusted ratings in the software space following the recent re-rating of the shares. Phillip Securities also cut Palo Alto Networks' (PANW) rating to Reduce from Neutral.

Barclays downgraded HubSpot (HUBS) to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged price target of $240. While the firm remains constructive on the company's long-term opportunity, it now believes the timing will take longer than expected.

Barclays downgraded Monday.com (MNDY) to Equal Weight from Overweight with an unchanged price target of $100. The firm believes the company's AI monetization story is gaining traction but remains in the "early innings."

Deutsche Bank downgraded C.H. Robinson (CHRW) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $153, down from $220. The firm says the shares could remain range-bound in the near term as investors assess the company's significant increase in leverage from the RXO (RXO) acquisition.

title: Spotify Stock Is Up Nearly 9% Since September 30 as Audiobooks Go Global. Here’s Where It Could Go by 2030
detail:
Spotify Stock Is Up Nearly 9% Since September 30 as Audiobooks Go Global. Here’s Where It Could Go by 2030
Wiltone Asuncion
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 3:53 AM MDT 5 min read
SPOT

Spotify Stock Is Up Nearly 9% Since September 30 as Audiobooks Go Global. Here's Where It Could Go by 2030 ©@inkdrop via Canva, @Bongkarngraphic from bongkarngraphic via Canva
Key Stats for Spotify Stock

Current Price: $529.14

Target Price (Mid): ~$1,040

Street Target: ~$594

Potential Total Return: ~97%

Annualized IRR: ~17% / year

What Happened?

Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) said on October 7 that it will take audiobooks from 22 markets to more than 180 by the end of 2026. On October 8, it renewed its licensing deal with Joe Rogan.

Shares rose about 5% intraday on October 7, though coverage split on why. TipRanks tied the move to a Bank of America note in which Jessica Reif Ehrlich reaffirmed a Buy and a $685 target, well above the Street mean of around $594. Other coverage pointed to the audiobook news. That week, Piper Sandler initiated coverage at Neutral with a $540 target.

The stock closed at $529.14 on October 9, up 8.6% from its September 30 close but 8.9% below where it started 2026. Spotify's investor relations materials set October 22, before the market opens, for third-quarter results.

Twelve Hours in Brazil, Add-On Only in Africa

New markets do not get the same deal. Eligible Premium subscribers in markets such as Brazil, Italy, Mexico, and Poland get 12 hours of audiobooks a month. That is below the roughly 15 hours co-CEO Gustav Söderström described Premium including. Across Africa, Asia, and Argentina, the paid Audiobooks+ add-on is the main way in.

The tiers fit how Söderström framed the business at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on September 9. Listening hours carry a cost, so Spotify controls how much Premium includes and sells to heavy users more. As he put it, "the margin is a managed outcome."

He also relayed co-CEO Alex Norström's line that maturing markets let Spotify keep "using the West to fund the East," where much of its growth now comes from.

Demand is building: Audiobooks+ has more than one million subscribers, and monthly audiobook listeners grew nearly 40% over the past year. Management's August 4 guide, set before any new market launched, already had a third-quarter gross margin at 32.9%. That is below the second quarter's 33.4%.

Spotify Premium & Ad-Supported Operating Revenue (TIKR)
Rogan Stays as Spotify Pays Podcasters From Premium

The renewal keeps Spotify's licensing and ad-sales rights on the No. 1 U.S. podcast by reach in the second quarter of 2026, according to Edison Research, though the show stays on other platforms. Spotify did not disclose terms. The Wall Street Journal reported they resemble the prior deal, which carried an estimated $250 million earnout.

Ads remain the slower line: Ad-Supported revenue rose 1% year over year to €446 million in the second quarter, while Premium grew 15%. Söderström's podcast plan leans on Premium. The Spotify Partner Program removed Spotify's own ads from podcasts for Premium listeners and pays creators from the Premium pool, which he said brought creators to upload video.

title: Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
detail:
Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
Joe Rogan stands in the octagon at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles after the light heavyweight bout between Alonzo Menifield of the United States and Iwo Baraniewski of Poland on Sept. 19. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
Wendy Lee
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 10:37 AM MDT 2 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Spotify on Thursday said it had renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who leads the audio company's most popular podcast, "The Joe Rogan Experience."

The podcast, which has 18 million followers on Spotify, has been the company's top podcast since 2020. The terms of the multiyear licensing deal were not disclosed. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, reported the deal had an estimated earnout of $250 million.

"The partnership with Spotify has been an amazing fit, and they're incredible to work with," Rogan said in a statement. "I'm extremely happy and excited to continue with them for years to come."

Rogan first entered into an exclusive multiyear podcast deal with Spotify in 2020 in a deal said to be worth $100 million. The partnership was key to driving podcast audiences to Spotify, which at the time was mostly known as a streaming music service.

Read more: Spotify digs in on podcasts with new Hollywood studios

In 2024, the company extended its partnership for "The Joe Rogan Experience" to be distributed on other platforms, and that will continue in the latest deal. Rogan's show was ranked as the top podcast last year on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Podcasts.

"Joe has built something incredibly enduring, and his show continues to resonate with a massive global audience because there's simply nothing else like it," said Jordan Newman, head of content partnerships at Spotify, in a statement.

"The Joe Rogan Experience" has run into controversy, spurring a Spotify boycott in 2022 led by Neil Young over concerns that Rogan and his guests were spreading misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines. Rogan also received criticism over his use of the N-word on past episodes of his show, for which he later apologized.

Read more: Joe Rogan apologizes for discussing doctored tweet on Spotify podcast

After the backlash, Spotify posted its content moderation rules and said it would add content advisory labels on COVID-related podcasts. Rogan also said he would do a better job of balancing different perspectives.

Young later returned to Spotify in 2024.

Over the past month, shares of this music-streaming service operator have returned -7.7%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Spotify falls in, has gained 9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Spotify is expected to post earnings of $3.12 per share, indicating a change of -18.5% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -4.6% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.85 points to a change of +16.5% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed -2.6%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $17.48 indicates a change of +26.2% from what Spotify is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -0.3%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.
